Half of active users read articles, most started guided journeys, and just under half completed exercises. Intuitive design, relevant symptom items, and reliable reminders are the design lessons drawn.
pmc-13279020:
Suhui Hu and colleagues report a 2026 study of a gut parasite in pigs on large farms. The parasite is Balantioides coli, a one celled germ that can also infect people. Pigs are its main host in farm settings. The team built a new test that reads two genes at once to tell strains apart.

They checked more than twelve hundred pig stool samples from three farms. About eighty eight percent held the parasite, and rates neared one hundred percent by five to six months of age. Gene reads found three types and a new form not seen before. Some types clustered in one region, which hints that farm place and practice shape spread.
pmc-13281320:

Switched-on platelets stick and clump, and the clumps choke the oxygenator.

Better design, they argue, could cut these events.
pmc-13282220:

The gap averaged roughly fifteen to twenty-two percent across three injury measures. Where strain peaked also shifted, and some deep brain regions showed rises up to about half. pmc-13282420:

pmc-13282620:
Tatiana Velásquez-Roa and co-authors present a 2026 software paper introducing Rosario, an algorithm and R package for analysing cyclical ecological data. That shift improves access and lets it work alongside other R packages for activity and overlap analysis. Unlike rivals, Rosario can analyse overlap among many identities at once, from individuals to whole communities. The authors say this gives a fuller view of temporal niches. They present standardisation in R as key to the method's continued use in ecology.
pmc-13282920:

Survival and relapse were tracked for three years with adjusted models. Patterns differed between myeloid and lymphoid leukemia types. Offspring donors showed weaker results in some groups. The study helps centers weigh donor choice when several relatives can donate.
pmc-13283220:
Spin waves and lattice vibrations merge into hybrid particles inside a layered magnet, Qili Li's tunneling experiments reveal in 2026. Such mixed waves are called magnon polarons and link magnetism with sound-like motion. Clear proof in metal magnets had been scarce before this work.

pmc-13283920:
Breathing failure tied to severe obesity anchors a 2026 clinical case from Sajedeh Zarghi and colleagues. Obesity hypoventilation syndrome leaves carbon dioxide high and oxygen low in blood. Late recognition can bring long intensive care stays and organ strain.

Linked harms span heart disease, diabetes, fatty liver, stroke, and sleep apnea. Early team-based care is presented as the way to cut harm and cost. Nutrition support teams play a named role in that early response.
pmc-13284420:
Yin Mo and co-authors share a research update, published in 2026, from the ADVANCE-ID trial network on drug-resistant bacterial and fungal infections. pmc-13285020:
Emma Bergstedt and Ann-Charlotte Nedlund trace health policy stories in Sweden in a 2026 study covering 1992 to 2024. pmc-13285320:
A 50-day-old boy with chlamydial lung infection and a blocked, collapsed lung lobe is the subject of a 2026 case report by Yuan Huang and colleagues. pmc-13285420: Mariam F. Farid and co-authors issue a correction, dated 2026, to a cat study of a cell-free spinal cord treatment for multiple sclerosis. The notice states that control images were reused from a sister study by the same team without clear notice. The authors say reuse kept the studies comparable and cut animal use, in line with welfare rules that favor fewer animals and kinder handling.
pmc-13285920:

pmc-13286520:

pmc-13287220:
Desmond Darko Asiedu and colleagues searched the maize genome in 2026 for regions that protect stalks against Fusarium rot, a soil-borne disease that cuts yields worldwide. Because many small effects shape resistance, the authors suggest selecting on the whole genome may serve breeding programmes better than single markers.
pmc-13287420:

The authors favour catheter treatment when anatomy suits it.
pmc-13287620:
Ahmed Sobhy and colleagues modelled power supply options in 2026 for Ras El-Hekma, a large coastal project in Egypt with peak demand of 28.8 megawatts and yearly use near 100.46 gigawatt-hours. pmc-13288720:

pmc-13289020:
Kelsey Hegarty and colleagues build a scale for coercive control in Australia. Their 2026 study deals with partner abuse of women. Past scales miss how abuse acts as a whole. The new scale is called C-CAS. It was built from older scales and expert views.

Severe control and tech threats formed two more. Scores held up well in tests. Fear rose with more severe patterns. More checks in new groups are still needed.
pmc-13289220:

pmc-13289320:

pmc-13290120:

The multi-task network learned from 8,260 knees belonging to 4,130 participants, grading osteoarthritis severity across all knees while predicting MRI-defined cartilage and meniscus damage in the mildest group. pmc-13290820:
When spine and hip bone scores disagree, the gap itself forecasts death in older women but not men, Rıdvan Erten and Mehmet Poyrazer report in a cohort study from 2026. Each unit of spine-minus-hip difference raised women's mortality hazard by about a quarter, while the men's estimate stayed small and borderline. pmc-13291420:
Medical students grow in trusted tasks during emergency training. Anne Marie Griebie leads a 2026 study of clerkship ratings. Such tasks are called Entrustable Professional Activities, or EPAs. Schools must know if growth curves follow learning theory.

The group held 481 students at one Minnesota school. Each did a four-week emergency rotation. Raters gave over seven thousand task ratings in total. Most task curves rose with the expected slowing shape. Five tasks broke that pattern and need a look. Six raters on six rounds gave solid score reliability. The data back the rating system’s design. Odd tasks may need better rater guidance.
pmc-13291720:
Betsabé Hernández-Santos and co-authors report a 2026 food science study on adding melon peel flour to extruded snacks made from soy protein and maize starch. pmc-13292320:
Akinori Miyashita and co-authors revisit a 2026 number with outsized influence: how much the APOE e4 gene variant raises Alzheimer's risk in Japanese people. pmc-13292520:
Stefanie Rosner and co-authors watch a 2026 group of heart failure patients through a single COVID-19 telecoaching module, checking whether knowledge and habits stuck. pmc-13293420:
Chiara De Poli and colleagues evaluate, in a 2026 study, how a co-designed information aid for people with dementia and family carers was put into practice in North-East England. Information needs in dementia often go unmet, despite policy stress on choice and control.

Interviews over time with a service manager and practitioners, plus a group talk with the design team, fed the review. Staff offered the leaflet often, though in varied ways, and some local tweaks appeared. The aid fit well into routine work and was welcomed by staff, who saw it as meeting a real need. Nine context levels and eight drivers helped explain how rollout went.
pmc-13293720:
Zhi-xiao Li and co-authors review, in a 2026 paper, how parvalbumin neurons, a key class of calming nerve cells, go wrong in depression. These cells keep the balance between excitation and inhibition in the brain, a balance known to break down in low mood.

pmc-13293820:
Blanca Gonzalez-Sánchez and co-authors survey, in a 2026 study, loneliness and leisure life among older adults who study at a university program in Extremadura, Spain, and live outside care homes. Loneliness is cast as one of the greatest challenges of later life.

pmc-13293920:
Adrián Idoate-Bayón and coauthors compare cooking skill and diet in a 2026 cross-sectional study of 592 Spanish adults, with 287 living with type 1 diabetes and 305 healthy controls. An 18-item scale measured culinary competence, covering skills like reading labels and adapting recipes. Models adjusted for social background factors.

Among controls, skill mainly meant fewer heavy sauces and cooking methods. Two skill groups emerged, and the expert group ate fewer ultra-processed foods at every income level.
pmc-13294220:
Kinga Skieresz-Szewczyk and Hanna Jackowiak trace tongue hardening in goose embryos in a 2026 tissue staining study. pmc-13294420:
Khaled El Ghonemy Said, Nada Mohammed Aggour, and Ahmed Ibrahim Basiony test drug injection into the cornea for stubborn fungal eye infection in a 2026 prospective series. Fungal keratitis causes 30–40% of cases in developing countries in the cited range and resists drops often. Patients averaged 57.19 years, mostly rural men with plant injury histories. Aspergillus led isolates at 52.4% in the reported share. Vision improved sharply by 3 months, and 19 patients, or 90.5%, healed fully. Direct delivery rescues cases that drops cannot reach.
pmc-13295520:
Ru-Ping Li, Fu-Shan Xue, and Yi Cheng raise questions about a hip fracture trial in a 2026 commentary. pmc-13295820:
Guo Wu and colleagues read gene activity behind stress behaviour in sea cucumbers in a 2026 study. The brainless animals answer threats by fleeing, clinging tight, or playing dead. Which pattern appears depends on the stress met, from dead tank-mates to cleaning water jets on farms.

Immune cells from stressed animals were profiled to trace the molecular switches behind each response. Comparing patterns across stress types separated shared alarm genes from response-specific ones. The work deepens understanding of how animals without a central brain still mount varied, fitting defences, and it may help farms cut stress losses in a valuable crop.
pmc-13295920:
Esias Ka Nanbe Bedingar and colleagues study, in 2026, paying vaccination workers by mobile money in Chad. Irregular cash allowances can sap motivation, so the team compare provinces that switched to digital payment with those that did not.

Surveys of 1,510 workers and dozens of interviews found higher motivation and job satisfaction where mobile payment was used. Barriers remained for remote staff with weak connectivity or low digital skills, pointing to training needs as such schemes expand.
pmc-13296220:
Elisée Mbombo and a large clinical team present, in 2026, four cases of previously healthy children with invasive disease from methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Such spreading infections are rarely reported in children in sub-Saharan Africa, yet they kill often when found late.

All four children had skin lesions and fever, with illness spreading across several body systems. Blood tests guided antibiotic choices, and long hospital stays with intensive care and source control ended in good outcomes. The authors urge suspicion when feverish infants show skin lesions with tender joints, since early aggressive care drives survival.
pmc-13296420:
Matteo De Simone and co-authors argue, in 2026, that the name chronic subdural hematoma misleads doctors about what the condition really is. Tissue evidence shows no natural subdural space exists, and the bleeding instead starts inside a fragile layer of the brain's outer membrane.

That view supports artery-blocking procedures and drugs aimed at vessel growth and clot breakdown. The authors urge new terms and team-based, mechanism-led care.
pmc-13299220:

The authors present the tool as a way to spend laboratory effort where confirmation is most likely.
pmc-13301320:
Lead in a mother's blood, more than her anemia, shadowed her toddler's development in Suriname, Anisma R. Gokoel and colleagues report in a 2026 cohort study. The Caribbean consortium cohort enrolled 755 pregnant women and assessed 644 children aged ten to twenty-six months with the Bayley scales. Lead gave the steadiest signal, predicting lower scores across domains, while mercury's links ran weaker. Selenium seemed to soften some metal effects. The authors warn against causal claims from this cross-sectional snapshot.
pmc-13303620:
Danial Mirzaee, Seyed Amir Malekpour, and Ata Kalirad propose a 2026 statistical method for estimating total population size from mark and recapture data. pmc-13304220:
Chukwuka Elendu and co-authors write a 2026 letter on liver shrinkage during immune drug hepatitis, responding to a fatal case report. Checkpoint drugs help liver cancer patients, but immune attack on the liver can turn deadly even when blood enzyme rises stay small.

pmc-13304320:

The method could speed adoption of digital frozen sand casting in aerospace and machine building while cutting pollution.
pmc-13304420:

pmc-13305320:

pmc-13306020:

pmc-13307020:

pmc-13307420:

pmc-13307920:

pmc-13308720:

pmc-13308820:

pmc-13308920:

pmc-13309020:
Guillermo Pérez Castro and co-authors build in 2026 finer models of free riding speed for bike traffic simulators, which now miss how slope, bends, crossings, and wind bend a rider pace. pmc-13310920:

pmc-13311220:

pmc-13311620:

pmc-13311820:

pmc-13311920:

pmc-13312020:

pmc-13312820:

pmc-13314320:

pmc-13314420:

pmc-13314920:

pmc-13316020:

pmc-13316220:

pmc-13317220:

pmc-13318720:

They found 1,070 papers from 67 countries and 1,584 institutions. The United States contributed 59.16 percent of publications and led citations. Managing linked conditions and tailoring treatment to specific groups also draw attention. The authors frame the map as a roadmap for future trials.
pmc-13318920:

pmc-13319420:
Jian Liu and co-authors give a broad review of epilepsy in a 2026 article on causes, body changes, and care. pmc-13320420:

pmc-13320520:

pmc-13325720:

pmc-13331920:

pmc-13333420:

pmc-13336420:

pmc-13336620:

pmc-13337020:

pmc-13396020:

Portable films from 814 critically ill adults, 4,259 images in total, were scored by trained clinicians blinded to clinical details. Patient groups ranged from ARDS to heart failure lung edema and airway protection cases.

Scores overlapped heavily among ARDS, heart edema, and lung scarring flare groups, since films look alike. Poor X-ray penetration inflated scores and wrecked accuracy.
pmc-13417720:
Antonello and colleagues reported in 2026 a hard-to-diagnose fever case at a public hospital in southern Brazil. A man in his sixties had high fever for over three weeks and severe leg muscle pain that limited walking. Tests for infection and cancer found no cause, meeting the formal idea of fever of unknown origin.

That pattern pointed to a body-wide inflammatory disease rather than infection. Rheumatology specialists supported adult-onset Still disease, a rare inflammatory disorder, using standard criteria. A low steroid dose helped partly, and a higher dose ended the fever and muscle pain quickly. The authors stress structured reasoning and careful reading of lab patterns where advanced tests are scarce.
pmc-13418520:
Roberto C French and co-authors capture brain activity and connectivity together while people watch a social film, in a 2026 neuroscience study. Viewers judged awkwardness, a cue to detecting social blunders and reading minds. Earlier work usually measured local activity or connections separately, and rarely tracked their change over time during natural scenes.

Sensorimotor activity rose with awkwardness ratings, while default network activity fell. Dynamic connections, especially involving the frontoparietal control network, explained extra variation beyond activity alone. Social judgement thus draws on both local firing and shifting network teamwork, the authors conclude, and methods should track both at once.
pmc-13419020:

pmc-13419220:

The mixes varied how many answers went missing, why they went missing, and how far question difficulty drifted. A standard linking method then tried to recover fair score matches under each mix. pmc-13419320:

The piece gives simulation leaders and change specialists a shared language for joint projects.
pmc-13421920:
Kadriyan and colleagues examined in 2026 whether handwash stations in health education institutions help students follow World Health Organization handwashing models. Knowledge alone often fails to change behavior, so they also watched the facilities themselves.

Observers judged the main washing infrastructure sufficient but found the supporting facilities, such as supplies around the sinks, substandard.
pmc-13422120: Correction: Saygin and colleagues correct their 2017 paper on CD55, a surface protein marking self-renewing, drug-resistant cells in endometrioid tumors of the ovary and uterus. The notice shows the original and corrected figures and states that conclusions and legends are unchanged. Corrected versions now appear online; the errors survive only in print and older downloads.
pmc-13424320:

pmc-13424420:

pmc-13424520:
Gil Genuth, Peter Stavrou, and Lukas D Iselin compare heel tendon surgery with and without a bioinductive collagen scaffold. The scaffold is a patch meant to coax healing. It was tested for insertional Achilles tendinopathy with Haglund deformity. pmc-13424620:

The package includes spike times, average waveforms, patient details, and electrode positions in a standard format, plus quality metrics and demonstrations that single neurons tune to film features. Decoding analyses even predict scenes from population activity. The authors offer the set as ready-made ground for machine learning.
pmc-13424820:

A summary analysis captured about eighty-four percent of all variation and grouped samples clearly by stage and site. The findings help growers pick harvest timing and origin for food, drug, and supplement uses.
pmc-13424920:
Duffy and colleagues tested in 2026 whether community health workers in rural Guatemala could manage high blood pressure safely with a phone app that guides each step of care. Blood pressure is a leading killer, and poor countries carry the heaviest load with the fewest doctors. The app, built on World Health Organization guidance, advised on drug dose changes, lifestyle counseling, and when to consult a physician.

Top-number blood pressure fell by about seven and a half points on average, and control rates rose. Eleven app errors occurred across more than two hundred visits, none harming a patient. The authors call the model ready for larger trials.
pmc-13425620:

The focus is the first assessment tier, the screening level used before deeper studies. A formal protocol, though not required, was judged worthwhile given the task's complexity.
pmc-13426020:
Theurich and colleagues published a 2026 study on when Brent geese leave for their breeding grounds. These geese stage each spring in the Wadden Sea before flying north. Leaving on the right wind can save energy and boost breeding success. The team tracked 43 tagged geese across seven spring seasons.

Damp air, by contrast, held birds back from leaving the staging site. Early in the season, geese picked their winds with great care. By early June, urgency grew and birds left on poorer winds. Weather records were matched hour by hour to each bird's position.
pmc-13426120:
Hu and colleagues tested in 2026 a metaverse rehab platform built for people who have survived colorectal cancer. Learnability, how easy the system is to pick up, scored lowest, while the quality of interaction scored highest. Interviewees liked the rich content and ease of access but said the controls still felt awkward to run.
pmc-13426320:
Alipour and colleagues published a 2026 study testing a suspected diet link to breast cancer. Advanced glycation end products form when food browns at high heat. Some past work tied these compounds to higher breast cancer risk. The team ran a careful case-control study across several centers in Iran.

Blood and tissue levels of the compounds also showed no real gap. Patients did report far less physical activity than the control group. The authors say their null result argues against a diet-compound link here. Larger studies that follow women over time could still revisit the question.
pmc-13426720:
Coelho and colleagues report a 2026 case of a 36-year-old motorcyclist with a severe vertical shear pelvic injury. The front joint of his pelvis had sprung apart by forty-two millimeters. The authors argue reinforced double plating suits very unstable front pelvic injuries.
pmc-13426920:

pmc-13427220:

The products are unsymmetric aromatic diols, molecules with two alcohol groups on a ring.

Together they steer the chemistry toward cross-coupling, instead of the unwanted self-coupling of identical fragments. pmc-13427320:

pmc-13427620:

The authors call for studies linking weather exposure data to drug outcomes, with confounding by illness and multiple medicines as the central hurdles. Where greener choices already match guidelines, they urge action now, backed by formulary and guideline reform.
pmc-13428120:

Scores held together very well, with a consistency measure of 0.937 on a scale where one is perfect, and repeat answers stayed steady. Patients who were married, active, and faithful to their medication reported better quality of life. Awwad concludes the Arabic survey is fit for clinic and research use across the region.
pmc-13429120:

pmc-13429220:

Equal cleaning power with less time and waste is the selling point.
pmc-13430820:

pmc-13432020:

pmc-13432820:

The authors also weigh fresh uses: bubble-based vaccines, bubble couriers for drug loads, and bubble strikes on tumors. A firm grasp of bubble traits, they argue, can seed new ways to spot, block, and treat infections.
pmc-13433320:

Old and mid-age crowds paired into joint teams that held from task to sleep, a tie fresh pairs lacked. In the hub, two cell layers grew more prone to team up as the memory aged. The authors read swift sorting and firming at work.
pmc-13433620:
Maria Laura Diniz Pereira and co-authors tested in 2026 how sour wear on tooth dentin cuts the grip of four filler pastes with tooth-tone mineral traits. One hundred twenty dentin bits from sound human molars split by wear path. Paths ran from a one-day sour soak to a soak plus five more days of wear rounds after the fill. One set took no wear at all. Each set split again by paste thinness and depth style.

Grip tests pulled the fills till they broke, and break kinds faced a scope check. Sour ground and paste kind each moved grip on their own, with no cross play. The long wear path sank grip for every paste against sound ground. Among thin pastes, the deep-fill one gripped harder. The plain thick pastes tied. Wear rounds hurt all bonds, the authors close.
pmc-13433820:

The symmetry constraint, built from steerable network layers, helps preserve fine anatomical detail while stripping noise and artifacts, the authors report. The model was trained and validated on the multi-site SynthRAD2025 dataset. It beat advanced rivals, including CycleGAN and a plain diffusion model. It won on structural fidelity, density accuracy, and quantitative scores. Images showed sharper soft tissue boundaries and more realistic bone, supporting more confident adaptive treatment planning.
pmc-13434420:
Jianping Xu and colleagues build a self running microbe system in 2026 that eats wood waste chemicals. Lignin leftovers are rich in useful ring compounds, yet they poison microbes and jam their inner pathways. The team hardened a workhorse germ and gave it smart gene switches.

Two more valued acids were made at high loads from the same stream. The design offers a template for green plants that run with little oversight.
pmc-13434820:

Memorization runs higher in medicine than in general text. Much of what is learned early sticks through later tuning, up to 87 percent in one check. Recall splits into helpful, dull, and harmful kinds. Harmful recall can leak private patient facts. The authors give steps to keep the helpful kind while cutting risk. Hospitals should test models before use.
pmc-13435820:

pmc-13436820:

Three pass cases rose from twelve percent to forty seven percent. Slide maker limits alone moved nothing. Steady audit plus reinforcement did the heavy lifting.
pmc-13436920:

pmc-13437320:

On a public medical device benchmark, the tool scored near-perfect marks for accuracy and for catching attacks. It missed forty of more than twenty-three thousand attack cases, a rate well inside the safety cap, and raised only twelve false alarms.
pmc-13439020:

pmc-13440220:

pmc-13440620:

The transcriptomic analysis also draws questions as the letter continues.
pmc-13442520:

Twisted models sent part of the pull sideways and forward at the foot end, a split the straight model never showed. Side force reached about 101 N and front force about 63 N in the twisted runs. Such spread may shape how the ankle and foot bear load with each step.
pmc-13442820:

pmc-13443420:

Trials had shown the drug works, but routine practice data were scarce. Their 2026 study follows 42 adults at three hospitals. It scores skin severity at the start, at four to six months, and past ten months. Side effects and time on the drug are logged too.

Severity scores fell steeply. The index dropped by about two thirds within six months, and further by the later check. At ten to twelve months, nine in ten patients still followed had cut their score by at least three quarters. Seven in ten had cut it by nine tenths. A third reported side effects, mostly skin, mouth, or infection issues, and three stopped the drug. Nearly three quarters stayed on treatment at last follow up.
pmc-13444320:
